card.name: Kromanti dance
card.tagline: Jamaican Maroon possession ceremony of Akan (Coromantee) origin
card.profile: Kromanti dance (Kromanti Play) is a Jamaican Maroon religious ceremony rooted in traditional African music and religious practices, especially those of the Akan people of Ghana (Wikipedia). The name derives from Kormantin, a historical slave fort on the Ghanaian coast. The ceremony invokes ancestral spirits through specialized drumming (gumbe, apinti), songs in the ritual Kromanti language (a creolized Akan dialect) and possession dances, led by a ritual specialist (fete-man/myal-man) (Wikipedia; Caribbean Languages).
card.insight: Ethnographer Kenneth Bilby's fieldwork documented spirit songs specific to individual ancestors, showing Kromanti invocations operate independently of later-adopted Christianity; the broader Maroon Heritage of Moore Town was proclaimed a UNESCO Masterpiece in 2003 and inscribed on the Representative List in 2008 (Caribbean Languages; UNESCO ICH).
